page: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadsv7 family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 2835 GB local disk and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core execution, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests, and reaching the top 10% in Geekbench multi-core metrics. Memory bandwidth is highly capable, with cached read-only operations and uncached write operations both scoring in the top 25%, though uncached large-block reads perform in the middle 50%. The processor supports advanced vector instructions including AVX-512 and AVX_VNNI, which contribute to top-tier performance in single-threaded compression and small-model LLM inference.

From a resource density perspective, the server offers high qualitative cost efficiency by combining a massive 2835 GB local storage allocation with a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. This eliminates the need for external storage attachments for data-intensive operations. The hardware profile is highly suited for relational databases, static web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale text processing or LLM inference workloads.
